previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient, a male with HLA-B27-positive ankylosing spondylitis, obesity, hypertension, asthma, and obstructive sleep apnea, was admitted for severe pain in the left sacroiliac joint that radiated to both hips, following completion of a prednisone taper. He reported inadequate relief from increased oral oxycodone and requested IV hydromorphone, which was initially administered. Concerns arose regarding opioid-induced hyperalgesia and behavioral components of pain, supported by inconsistent physical findings and nursing observations of normal activity when unobserved. The medical team decided against continued IV narcotics, continued his home oral opioid regimen, and recommended follow-up with his primary care provider. The patient understood the risks but chose to leave the hospital against medical advice.
problems: Ankylosing spondylitis of unspecified sites in spine

Brief Hospital Course:
Mr. ___ is a ___ year old male with PMH of hypertension, 
obesity, ankylosing spondylitis, OSA on CPAP, presenting with 
acute on chronic neck pain admitted for pain management. 
Problems addressed during his hospitalization are as follows:

#Neck Pain
#Ankylosing spondylitis:
Patient with ankylosing spondylitis and frequent episodes of 
pain, in variable locations, for which he takes chronic opioids 
and prednisone taper. Initially presented to ED for neck pain, 
was discharged, and subsequently returned after developing 
nausea and vomiting x1 while commuting home in his car. Cause of 
this flare is unclear, may have been exacerbated by reported 
""slip"" in shower around onset of flare during which he endorses 
straining his neck and hit his right knee. Lack of neurologic 
symptoms, resolution of nausea/vomiting, and unremarkable 
preliminary CTA head/neck are reassuring. Patient received 2 
doses of IV dilaudid in the emergency department, otherwise did 
not receive or request any additional IV narcotics. Continued 
home prednisone, oxycodone, oxycontin, lidocaine. Trialed 
ketorolac which was discontinued prior to discharge per patient 
request, noted developing gas/GI discomfort. Tolerated regular 
diet at time of discharge with resolution of nausea and no 
additional episodes of vomiting.

#GERD: Continued home omeprazole.

#OSA: Continued home CPAP.

#Asthma: Continued home albuterol, ipratropium.
